assets.title: A task for every client email
assets.content:
Subject: A task for every client email
Preview text: Keep scheduled team work visible from the inbox.

Give each client email a clear next action

Hi there,

Missive is a collaborative email client and shared team inbox built around the conversation. Any email can become a task, with scheduled team work for today, tomorrow, and next week visible from the inbox.

That gives a team a concrete next action on the client email and a shared view of upcoming work, without leaving the inbox.

At Scale CPA, Chris Wattinger said mentions helped the team hand the drafting or processing of client emails to someone else. For their client-services workflow, that capability brought enormous value.

Missive offers a 30-day free trial, with no credit card required.

Try Missive free → https://mail.missiveapp.com/#signup

- Missive

asset_metadata.single_idea: If client emails pass between teammates, Missive can keep the work attached to the email: turn it into a task, then use a teammate mention to hand off drafting or processing.

selected_brief.selection_reason: Client-email handoff is the strongest documented operational use for this reader: it combines a concrete inbox task mechanism with proof from a client-services firm and supports a simple first-product introduction.

value_case.reader_benefit: If client emails need input from different teammates, the agency can keep the email connected to a visible task and hand drafting or processing to a teammate instead of treating the message as an isolated inbox item.
value_case.mechanism: Missive can turn any email into a task and show what people are working on today, tomorrow, and next week without leaving the inbox. Scale CPA described using teammate mentions to hand off the drafting or processing of client emails.
decision_conditions: A mention-based handoff requires the intended teammate to be mentionable in the same workspace.
The evidence does not establish which task or mention capabilities are included in the free trial.

claim_conditions: Present Scale CPA's statement as that customer's experience, not a typical or guaranteed result.
Keep the task claim to turning an email into a task and seeing scheduled team work from the inbox.
The free trial lasts 30 days and requires no credit card; do not infer its feature entitlements.
Do not promise: No claim that internal notes stay hidden from clients
Do not promise: No claim that all client inboxes can be consolidated into one tool
Do not promise: No multi-channel (SMS/WhatsApp/Instagram/Messenger) chat claim
Do not promise: No claim of growth, zero disruption, headcount savings, or being cheaper/better than the incumbent
Do not promise: No AI assistant, API/MCP, SSO or automation-rule entitlement implied for the trial
Do not promise: No pricing detail (per-user/month figures) introduced, since the single next step is the trial itself, not a paid plan decision
This is a documented-use draft, not proof of the broader audience hypothesis or recipient fit.
selected_brief.job: Make one client-email coordination workflow concrete enough that a new buyer wants to start a low-commitment evaluation of Missive.
selected_brief.single_idea: If client emails pass between teammates, Missive can keep the work attached to the email: turn it into a task, then use a teammate mention to hand off drafting or processing.
selected_brief.mechanism: Show the workflow in one line: a client email becomes a task that remains visible from the inbox, while a teammate mention hands off its drafting or processing. Use Scale CPA as narrow proof that a client-services team found this mention-based handoff valuable.
selected_brief.belief_shift: Before: Missive is an unfamiliar shared-inbox product. After: the reader sees a specific way it could organize a client-email handoff and knows they can begin evaluating Missive for 30 days without a credit card.
must_not_say: No claim that internal notes stay hidden from clients.
No claim that all client inboxes can be consolidated into one tool.
No multi-channel SMS, WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, or live-chat claim.
No claim of growth, zero disruption, headcount savings, time savings, faster responses, or being cheaper or better than an incumbent.
No AI assistant, API, MCP, SSO, or automation-rule entitlement implied for the trial.
No pricing detail, since the next step is the trial rather than a paid-plan decision.
Do not claim that task creation or teammate mentions are available in the trial; exact trial entitlements are not established.
Do not generalize Scale CPA's experience to agencies overall.
Do not introduce integration count, adoption count, security, compliance, migration, setup effort, or competitor comparisons.
Do not assert that the recipient currently forwards emails, misses messages, uses a named incumbent, or manages several distinct client inboxes.
selected_brief.objection: Starting an evaluation may feel like unnecessary commitment before the team knows whether Missive fits; answer only with the documented 30-day trial and no-credit-card requirement.
selected_brief.call_to_action: Try Missive free for 30 days — no credit card required.
selected_brief.next_step_decision: After a time-bounded evaluation, decide whether Missive merits further consideration for the team's client-email workflow.
selected_brief.next_step_value: The signup starts a documented 30-day free trial of Missive without requiring a credit card.
selected_brief.next_step_limit: The evidence does not establish the trial's feature entitlements, setup or migration effort, or whether Missive fits the agency's broader client-inbox operation.
selected_brief.subject_strategy: Earn the open by naming the concrete client-email handoff opportunity, not by using a generic collaboration promise, price comparison, or unsupported pain claim.

reader_verdicts.what_it_sells: Missive is a collaborative email and shared-inbox app that would let my team turn client emails into tasks and see scheduled work inside the inbox.
reader_verdicts.relevance_feedback: The profile establishes that I manage multiple client inboxes, so coordinating next actions on client email is potentially relevant. The email additionally assumes my team needs handoffs and scheduled work inside the inbox; whether that is a current problem, and whether Missive can keep distinct clients properly separated, are unknown.
assumed_experiences: Profile-supported: I manage multiple client inboxes for an agency.
Email-only: My team needs every client email to have a task or scheduled next action.
Email-only: Client-email drafting or processing is handed between team members.
Email-only: Keeping upcoming work inside the inbox would improve my workflow.
reader_verdicts.problem_now: Clear next actions and team handoffs could matter in my work, but the profile does not establish that this is causing trouble now or that I need to change systems.
reader_verdicts.stopped_at: At Scale CPA, Chris Wattinger said mentions helped the team hand the drafting or processing of client emails to someone else.
reader_verdicts.biggest_doubt: I cannot picture how this works across several distinct client inboxes: whether I can separate clients, assign an owner and due date, and review upcoming work without mixing accounts. The vague testimonial does not answer that.
reader_verdicts.to_click_it_would_have_to: I would have clicked if this email had shown, in one concrete sentence, how an agency turns an email in one client inbox into an assigned, dated task and views it separately from other clients' work.
fixes: Rewrite "Any email can become a task, with scheduled team work for today, tomorrow, and next week visible from the inbox" to state the actual action a user takes and what task details or views are available, without implying unsupported capabilities.

Replace "That gives a team a concrete next action on the client email and a shared view of upcoming work, without leaving the inbox" with an agency-specific example involving one of several client inboxes.
Cut or make specific "For their client-services workflow, that capability brought enormous value"; "enormous value" does not tell me what improved.

brief.interpretation: Treat this as a single acquisition email introducing Missive to a solution-aware agency team that may handle client emails collaboratively. Because the recipient relationship is unknown, the argument conditionally presents one documented workflow—turning a client email into a task and handing drafting or processing to a teammate—then asks for one action: start the 30-day free trial.
brief.reader:
Selected audience: Agency managing multiple client inboxes.
Research context describes some members of this market, not this recipient's installed tools or experiences. Follow the campaign request when it scopes the job.
Observed situation (inferred; check applicability): The corpus describes teams that operate shared inboxes such as help@ or info@ and triage conversations across one or more of those shared inboxes as a team, with internal comment and assignment features; it does not confirm this is an agency managing several distinct client inboxes.
brief.promise: Missive gives teams handling client emails a way to turn an email into a task and use a teammate mention to hand off drafting or processing without leaving the inbox workflow.
brief.orientation: Missive is a shared-inbox email tool that agency staff can use to assign and discuss client emails as a team.
brief.arc: Move the reader from knowing Missive only as another shared-inbox option to understanding one concrete client-email handoff workflow and seeing a low-commitment way to evaluate the product.
brief.sequence_rationale: One email should make one operational use case tangible rather than cataloguing features. E16 establishes the task mechanism, E10 supplies closely matched customer proof for mention-based handoff of client-email work, and E4 answers the immediate commitment concern. No researched recipient pain or incumbent workflow is established, so the email should use a conditional application rather than manufacture a failure story. The evidence establishes a free trial but not the availability of the task and mention capabilities within that trial, so the CTA should promise only the documented 30-day trial, not a specific in-trial entitlement.

emails.selection_reason: Client-email handoff is the strongest documented operational use for this reader: it combines a concrete inbox task mechanism with proof from a client-services firm and supports a simple first-product introduction.

value_case.reader_benefit: If client emails need input from different teammates, the agency can keep the email connected to a visible task and hand drafting or processing to a teammate instead of treating the message as an isolated inbox item.
value_case.mechanism: Missive can turn any email into a task and show what people are working on today, tomorrow, and next week without leaving the inbox. Scale CPA described using teammate mentions to hand off the drafting or processing of client emails.
decision_conditions: A mention-based handoff requires the intended teammate to be mentionable in the same workspace.
The evidence does not establish which task or mention capabilities are included in the free trial.

claim_conditions: Present Scale CPA's statement as that customer's experience, not a typical or guaranteed result.
Keep the task claim to turning an email into a task and seeing scheduled team work from the inbox.
The free trial lasts 30 days and requires no credit card; do not infer its feature entitlements.
Do not promise: No claim that internal notes stay hidden from clients
Do not promise: No claim that all client inboxes can be consolidated into one tool
Do not promise: No multi-channel (SMS/WhatsApp/Instagram/Messenger) chat claim
Do not promise: No claim of growth, zero disruption, headcount savings, or being cheaper/better than the incumbent
Do not promise: No AI assistant, API/MCP, SSO or automation-rule entitlement implied for the trial
Do not promise: No pricing detail (per-user/month figures) introduced, since the single next step is the trial itself, not a paid plan decision
This is a documented-use draft, not proof of the broader audience hypothesis or recipient fit.
emails.job: Make one client-email coordination workflow concrete enough that a new buyer wants to start a low-commitment evaluation of Missive.
emails.single_idea: If client emails pass between teammates, Missive can keep the work attached to the email: turn it into a task, then use a teammate mention to hand off drafting or processing.
emails.mechanism: Show the workflow in one line: a client email becomes a task that remains visible from the inbox, while a teammate mention hands off its drafting or processing. Use Scale CPA as narrow proof that a client-services team found this mention-based handoff valuable.
emails.belief_shift: Before: Missive is an unfamiliar shared-inbox product. After: the reader sees a specific way it could organize a client-email handoff and knows they can begin evaluating Missive for 30 days without a credit card.
must_not_say: No claim that internal notes stay hidden from clients.
No claim that all client inboxes can be consolidated into one tool.
No multi-channel SMS, WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, or live-chat claim.
No claim of growth, zero disruption, headcount savings, time savings, faster responses, or being cheaper or better than an incumbent.
No AI assistant, API, MCP, SSO, or automation-rule entitlement implied for the trial.
No pricing detail, since the next step is the trial rather than a paid-plan decision.
Do not claim that task creation or teammate mentions are available in the trial; exact trial entitlements are not established.
Do not generalize Scale CPA's experience to agencies overall.
Do not introduce integration count, adoption count, security, compliance, migration, setup effort, or competitor comparisons.
Do not assert that the recipient currently forwards emails, misses messages, uses a named incumbent, or manages several distinct client inboxes.
emails.objection: Starting an evaluation may feel like unnecessary commitment before the team knows whether Missive fits; answer only with the documented 30-day trial and no-credit-card requirement.
emails.call_to_action: Try Missive free for 30 days — no credit card required.
emails.next_step_decision: After a time-bounded evaluation, decide whether Missive merits further consideration for the team's client-email workflow.
emails.next_step_value: The signup starts a documented 30-day free trial of Missive without requiring a credit card.
emails.next_step_limit: The evidence does not establish the trial's feature entitlements, setup or migration effort, or whether Missive fits the agency's broader client-inbox operation.
emails.subject_strategy: Earn the open by naming the concrete client-email handoff opportunity, not by using a generic collaboration promise, price comparison, or unsupported pain claim.

brief.voice_notes: Use Missive's short, functional style. Explain what the workflow does rather than praising it. Avoid hype, broad category claims, and fictional recipient circumstances.
